text: dsh-ontology 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的持久化知识图谱插件，适合需要让 agent 跨会话保存结构化领域知识的场景。它在 DSH 中注册定义、断言、查询和撤回四个工具，并将当前词汇摘要加入系统提示。用户可以声明类和带类型的关系，按领域与值域校验实体事实，通过对称、逆关系和传递关系推导事实，也可按类、文本、三元组、邻域或路径查询。图谱保存在 DSH storage domain；无需额外 API key，需支持 storage-domain 的 DSH 环境。

dsh-ontology adds a typed graph to DSH. Its tools define classes and relations, validate facts, query entities or paths, and retract records. Queries can infer inverse, symmetric, and transitive facts. A prompt section can summarize the vocabulary. It uses DSH storage and needs no API key.
想让 DSH 记住跨会话的实体和它们之间的关系。
我需要给领域知识定义类别和关系类型，再验证新事实是否符合。
有没有办法从已有关系自动推出传递关系或反向关系？
想按类别、关键词或三元组条件搜索知识图谱里的记录。
帮我查看两个实体之间通过哪些关系连接起来。
需要删除某个实体时，也一并清理提到它的事实。
I want a durable graph where an agent can store typed entities and relationships between sessions.
How can I check that a new fact matches the classes and relation constraints I defined?
I need to find the shortest relation path between two entities in stored domain knowledge.
Can queries return facts implied by inverse, symmetric, or transitive relations?
dsh-ontology 的功能「定义本体词汇」：通过 ontology_define 声明类、父类和带类型的关系，并检查引用与约束；一次调用可按多轮解析前后依赖的定义。
dsh-ontology 的功能「断言实体与事实」：通过 ontology_assert 写入实体和关系事实，按已声明的领域和值域校验，并可合并重复实体。
dsh-ontology 的功能「查询图谱」：ontology_query 支持词汇、统计、实体、事实、邻域、路径和图谱导出模式，可选返回推导事实。
dsh-ontology 的功能「关系推理」：查询可根据逆关系、对称关系和传递关系派生新事实，并标记推导来源及达到上限时的不完整状态。
dsh-ontology 的功能「撤回记录」：ontology_retract 可删除词汇、实体或单条事实；删实体会级联删除引用它的事实，仍被依赖的词汇会被拒绝删除。
dsh-ontology 使用 maxInferred 限制每次读取派生事实的数量；达到上限时结果会标记为不完整，可在插件配置中提高上限。

dsh-ontology README · dsh-ontology：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A typed, inference-capable **ontology** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — durable domain knowledge the agent declares, asserts against, and queries under schema constraints.

dsh-ontology README · dsh-ontology：Most agent memory is a bag of strings: the agent writes prose, later reads prose, and nothing ever tells it that what it just recorded contradicts what it recorded last week. This plugin gives the agent a **vocabulary it must respect**. You declare what kinds of things exist and how they may relate; every claim is then checked against that model before it is stored, and claims that follow from other claims are derived rather than repeated.

dsh-ontology README · dsh-ontology：```
ontology_define   declare classes and typed relations   (the TBox)
ontology_assert   record entities and facts             (the ABox, validated)
ontology_query    look things up, traverse, infer
ontology_retract  remove, with dependency protection

dsh-ontology README · Why a TBox, not a notes file：| | notes-style memory | dsh-ontology |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | free text | classes, typed relations, entities, triples |
| Bad input | silently stored | rejected, naming the constraint it broke |
| Implied facts | restated by hand, drift apart | derived on read from `transitive` / `symmetric` / `inverseOf` |
| Retraction | orphaned prose lingers | facts cascade with their entity; derived facts vanish with their premise |
| Reading it back | grep and hope | query by class (subclass-aware), triple pattern, neighbourhood, or shortest path |
section: Why a TBox, not a notes file

text:
dsh-ontology README · Why a TBox, not a notes file：The constraint is the point. When the agent asserts `ada depends_on api` and `depends_on` is declared `Component -> Component`, it gets back:

```
REJECTED ada depends_on api: ada is not in the domain of depends_on
  (requires one of: Component; has: Person)
```

That is a real signal — either the claim is wrong, or the model of the domain is incomplete. Free-text memory can produce neither.
section: Why a TBox, not a notes file

text:
dsh-ontology README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-ontology
dsh --profile <name>
```

Or from a checkout / git host:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add ./dsh-ontology
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:tancheng33/dsh-ontology
```

dsh-ontology README · Install：> A `github:` install builds from source, so pnpm ≥10 needs the build allowlisted. Add `allowBuilds: { dsh-ontology: true }` to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and re-run, and pin a commit (`#<sha>`) so a later push cannot silently change what runs. Installing from npm needs no allowance.

dsh-ontology README · Install：The ontology persists through the storage stack (`dsh-storage` + `dsh-storage-json` + `dsh-storage-domain`) that `dsh-base` ships since **dsh 0.1.5**, so the bundle contributes only its own `ontology` row. It therefore needs dsh ≥ 0.1.5-rc.2; on older harnesses add the three storage rows to your profile patch yourself. Data lands in `$DSH_HOME/storages/<domain>.json`.

dsh-ontology README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | `ontology` | Storage domain name; one name is one isolated graph. Must match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/`. |
| `strict` | `true` | Reject facts that violate the vocabulary. `false` stores them with the violations recorded, for exploratory modelling. |
| `inference` | `true` | Allow queries to return entailed facts. |
| `maxInferred` | `20000` | Cap on derived facts per read. Past it, results carry `inferenceTruncated: true` and the rendered text says so; raise it for graphs with large transitive closures. |
| `promptSection` | `true` | Contribute the vocabulary summary to the system prompt. |
| `promptMaxTerms` | `60` | Upper bound on terms in that summary. |
| `promptOrder` | `150` | Where the section lands in the assembled prompt. |
| `defaultLimit` / `maxLimit` | `50` / `500` | Query result sizes. |
| `maxEntities` / `maxFacts` | `20000` / `100000` | Capacity guards; a write past the bound fails loudly. |

dsh-ontology README · Configuration：Running two isolated graphs is just two rows:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ontology-team
      name: dsh-ontology
      config: { domain: team_ontology, strict: true, inference: true, maxInferred: 20000,

(A patch replaces a row's whole `config`, so restate every key.)

dsh-ontology README · A worked example：**Declare the vocabulary.** Order does not matter — entries are resolved by repeated passes, so a subclass may precede its parent and a relation may precede its inverse.

```jsonc
// ontology_define
{
  "classes": [
    { "id": "Service", "subClassOf": ["Component"] },

**Assert instances.** Entities are created before the facts of the same call, so one call introduces an individual and its relationships together.

dsh-ontology README · A worked example：```
connected in 3 step(s):
  ada owns api
  api depends_on auth
  auth depends_on pg

dsh-ontology README · Query modes：| Mode | Answers |
|---|---|
| `schema` | What vocabulary exists? (Start here.) |
| `stats` | How big is the graph, and how much is inferable? |
| `entities` | Which individuals are in class X (including its subclasses), or match text Y? |
| `facts` | Which triples match this pattern? Each omitted position is a wildcard. |
| `neighbors` | What surrounds this entity, out to depth N? |
| `path` | How are these two entities connected? |
| `dump` | Everything asserted — terms, entities, facts — as data, for export or backup. Re-import is `ontology_define` + `ontology_assert`. |

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Subsumption.** `subClassOf` is transitive: an entity declared `Service` is also a `Component`, so it satisfies a `Component` domain and is returned by a `Component` query. Cycles are refused at definition time — a cycle would make "is an X" unfalsifiable for every class on it.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Domain and range.** A relation's `domain` constrains subjects, its `range` constrains objects, both closed under subsumption. An empty list means unconstrained, which is the honest encoding of "not yet decided" rather than a silent allow-all.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Entity vs literal.** `rangeKind: "literal"` makes a relation attribute-valued (a version string, a date). A literal-valued relation can be neither symmetric, transitive, nor inverted — the derived triple would have a literal in subject position — and that incoherence is refused at definition time rather than producing nonsense later.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Functional cardinality.** A `functional` relation admits at most one object per subject. A second, different object is a `functional-conflict`, not a silent overwrite. Re-asserting the *same* object stays idempotent.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Entailment.** `transitive`, `symmetric`, and `inverseOf` are applied to a fixpoint, so the rules compose (the inverse of a transitive relation is itself closed transitively). Entailed facts are **derived on read and never stored** — retract a premise and everything resting on it disappears, with no stale derivation left behind. Each carries `via` naming the rule that produced it.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Retraction safety.** Retracting an entity cascades to every fact mentioning it. Retracting a *term* is refused while anything still depends on it — a class that still classifies an entity or appears in a relation signature, a relation still asserted — and the refusal names the dependent.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Redefinition safety.** Redefining a term replaces it wholesale, so the stored facts are re-checked against the would-be vocabulary: narrowing a domain or range, flipping `rangeKind`, adding `functional` over a subject that already has two objects, or cutting a class out of a `subClassOf` chain that facts rely on is refused under `strict`, naming the facts it would break. Under `strict: false` it is applied and the damage is returned as warnings.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Duplicate guard.** A new entity whose id differs from an existing one only by case, separators, or a `ns:` prefix (`mod:api` beside `api`), or whose label is an existing id, is accepted but comes back with a `possible-duplicate` warning that spells out the merge to run. The store cannot know whether they are one thing, so it says so instead of guessing.

dsh-ontology README · The rules it enforces：**Merging.** When two ids turn out to name one individual, `ontology_assert` with `merges: [{ from, into }]` rewrites every fact about `from` onto `into`, unions the classes, keeps `into`'s label and comment (filling gaps from `from`), and drops `from`. Rewrites that collide with existing triples collapse; a rewrite that would violate the vocabulary (a `functional` relation seeing two objects) refuses the merge under `strict`.

dsh-ontology README · Scale：Reads are indexed and memoized per write generation: the first query after a write derives the closure once (a worklist fixpoint over an adjacency index, not a quadratic scan), and every query until the next write reuses it. Writes keep a subject index so a `functional` check costs the subject's degree, not a table scan. On a 21k-entity / 101k-fact synthetic dependency graph (`pnpm bench 20000 3`, Apple Silicon):

dsh-ontology README · Scale：| Operation | Before 0.2 | 0.2 |
|---|---|---|
| assert 101k facts in batches of 500 | 340 s | 0.5 s |
| first inferred query after a write | > 6 s at 10k facts | 0.1 s |
| repeated inferred queries | > 6 s each | < 1 ms |
| shortest path, depth 8, inferred | > 6 s | 16 ms |

Entailment stops at `maxInferred` derived facts and says so rather than silently returning a prefix of the closure.

dsh-ontology README · Scale：The storage medium is the default `dsh-storage-json` unit (one JSON document per domain, rewritten atomically per write). For graphs in the tens of thousands of facts, override the `storage-json` row in your profile patch with `dsh-storage-sqlite`; the plugin does not care which backend serves its domain.

The prompt section is assembled once per turn by the harness, so vocabulary defined during a turn appears in the standing context from the next turn on.

dsh-ontology README · Using the reasoning core on its own：The rule engine is pure — no IO, no storage, no Cordis — and ships as its own entry point, so it can be used outside a harness:

```ts
import { entail, findPath, validateFactInput } from 'dsh-ontology/ontology'
```

dsh-ontology README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test        # 60 unit tests: rules, tools, prompt section
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build

`tests/memory-domain.ts` is an in-memory stand-in for one open storage domain, so the store and the tools are tested end to end — real validation, real entailment, real tool results — without a backend.

dsh-ontology README · Development：`pnpm smoke` is the test the unit suite cannot be. It installs the packed tarball into a fresh dsh profile created from the shipped `headless` template (so `dsh-base` is present), boots it against a scripted local LLM that speaks both wire formats the harness has used, drives `ontology_define` → `ontology_assert` → `ontology_query` with inference, then boots a second time over the same `$DSH_HOME` to check persistence and that the prompt section now carries the vocabulary. No network beyond the npm registry, no API key. `DSH_VERSION` picks the harness (CI runs the oldest supported line and `next`); `DSH_BIN` reuses an installed one; `SMOKE_PLUGIN_SPEC=dsh-ontology@0.1.0` demonstrates that the test catches the duplicate-storage-row boot crash of that release.

dsh-ontology README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.1.5-rc.2` (dsh-base must ship the storage stack)
- Node `^22.19 || >=24`
